I first watched Naruto when I was about four years old. By that time, it had already been airing for around three years, but I quickly caught on. By the time Shippuden came out, I was already a massive Naruto fan. It's extremely hard to believe how fast those 10 years of Shippuden passed—and even more unreal that it’s already been nearly a decade since it ended.

Thinking back to when I waited a whole week for each new episode, I couldn't even comprehend the idea of Shippuden having 500 episodes if someone had told me at the beginning it's going to be that long. Watching anime over such a long period is a completely different experience compared to binge-watching. The story just hits differently, and the emotions are incomparable. The pacing, fillers, and storytelling all felt natural. I enjoyed the fillers as much as the canon episodes and would never skip them like some people do—they just added depth to the story and the world of the anime.

I’m missing some key moments, but to include them all, we’d need something like a "Top 300 Naruto Moments" list. Some of the most unforgettable moments for me include how Naruto changed Nagato’s way of thinking, the fight where Konan nearly killed Obito, how the Legendary Sannin found the three kids and Jiraiya raised them, all of Orochimaru’s attempts to kidnap Naruto, Sasuke’s fight with the Eight-Tails, Naruto breaking through the barriers after training and joining the Great War, Shikamaru’s father’s death, Obito’s death, Neji’s death, Asuma’s death, Grandma Chiyo’s death, Rin’s death—and so many other unforgettable losses.

Then there was Sakura "confessing" to Naruto, Naruto vs. Neji in the Chunin Exams, Sasuke finally killing that bastard Danzo, Sasuke learning the truth about Itachi, Sasuke and revived Itachi’s reunion, Naruto's training rasengan, Tsunade giving Naruto her necklace, Naruto training moments with Jiraya, Naruto mastering Rasen-Shuriken and using it for the first time, annoucement of Jiraya's death to Tsunade and Naruto, and countless other memorable moments.

This show has been great, a true masterpiece and lifework dedication from Masashi Kishimoto and all other participating animators and artists. Thank you :)

raw_comment:
Naruto/Sasuke fight was the absolute best. Kishimoto said that he knew the final battle/scenes for Naruto from the very beginning, which is why these final episodes/chapters were so well-done and well-written. You may not agree with Sasuke but you should be able to understand his reasoning here, and it's consistent with his character.

Also about the discussion, Sasuke is not trying to be "good". He's trying to be effective because he's completely goal-oriented. And his goal is world peace. The reason why he believes his is the correct option is because every other option has failed. Acting as an "Itachi for the world" is the one option which he's seen personally work in his own life, so he thinks it's a viable path for the world as well. If another better option was presented that Sasuke could see for himself, he would absolutely pursue that as well. This is not a path that Sasuke *wants* to do but one that he feels he *needs* to in order to fulfill that goal of world peace.

As a solution, Sasuke has the most logical plan for world peace.
